items.name: tailings
items.per: per kg of natural uranium produced (mining plus milling)
items.note: Tab. 13, world row: 0.56 m3 of tailings per kg Unat, at a tailings density of 1800 kg/m3 (footnote 46) that is about 1'008 kg of tailings per kg of natural uranium. The dataset's includedProcesses says its land use is 'mostly tailings', but the excerpt gives no area or occupation time, so this quantity cannot be turned into an Occupation or Transformation flow and is reported here rather than invented.

gaps: The report gives the direct energy for URANIUM MINING AND MILLING TOGETHER ('Foerderung und -aufbereitung'). This dataset is the milling step alone, so the energy above is an upper bound for it; the excerpt offers no split.
Tab. 12 has no 'world' row - the world average had to be computed from the country rows and the 2009 production volumes.

None of the ~67 elementary flows this dataset actually carries can be read: the report says explicitly 'Anlagen- oder laenderspezifische Angaben zu Emissionsparametern, Landverbrauch, Betriebsmitteln sowie Bedarf an Transporten und Infrastruktur sind ... nicht vorhanden' and falls back on Dones et al. (2009), which is not in this excerpt.
No radioactive emissions to air or water (radon-222, uranium, radium, thorium), which are the dominant flows of a uranium milling dataset.
No chemicals for leaching, no land occupation for the tailings pond, no transport and no infrastructure.
No water use, although the dataset's includedProcesses mentions mining water.
